alt.en: Part of a printed map in black on buff paper: islands and winding creeks between the Coosaw River and the sea, with water drawn in fine wavy lines. Beaufort is marked on Port Royal Island; St. Helena Island, at the centre, has "Church" and, on its eastern side, "Coffin". At right, "St. Helena Sound"; at bottom, "Port Royal Entrance" and "Hilton Head". Handwritten notes in blue pencil mark forts and their guns.
alt.es: Parte de un mapa impreso en negro sobre papel ocre: islas y caños sinuosos entre el río Coosaw y el mar, con el agua dibujada en finas líneas onduladas. Beaufort aparece en la isla de Port Royal; la isla de St. Helena, en el centro, lleva "Church" y, en su lado este, "Coffin". A la derecha, "St. Helena Sound"; abajo, "Port Royal Entrance" y "Hilton Head". Unas notas manuscritas a lápiz azul señalan fuertes y sus cañones.

caption.en: St. Helena Island and Beaufort on a map of 1861 compiled from the U.S. Coast Survey, with "Coffin" printed on the island's eastern side: Charles Pickard Ware made his collection, this song among it, chiefly at Coffin's Point, the plantation a letter of March 1862 places "about fifteen miles east of Beaufort, on St. Helena Island, coast of St. Helena Sound".
caption.es: La isla de St. Helena y Beaufort en un mapa de 1861 hecho a partir del U.S. Coast Survey (el servicio de costas de Estados Unidos), con "Coffin" impreso en el lado este de la isla: Charles Pickard Ware reunió su colección, con esta canción, sobre todo en Coffin's Point, la plantación que una carta de marzo de 1862 sitúa "about fifteen miles east of Beaufort, on St. Helena Island, coast of St. Helena Sound" (a unas quince millas al este de Beaufort, en la isla de St. Helena, en la costa del estrecho de St. Helena).

source: Map of St. Helena Sound, and the coast between Charleston and Savannah, compiled from the U.S. Coast Survey (Boston: A. Williams & Co., 1861; lith. by C. D. Andrews & Co., Boston), detail of the Port Royal islands
library: Boston Public Library, Norman B. Leventhal Map & Education Center

alt.en: A printed book page headed "xvi SLAVE SONGS OF THE", beginning "The same songs are used for rowing as for snouting." (a misprint for "shouting") and "I know only one pure boat-song, the fine lyric, "Michael row the boat ashore" (No. 31)", then Mr. Ware's note that "two measures are to be sung to each stroke".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el encabezado "xvi SLAVE SONGS OF THE", que empieza "The same songs are used for rowing as for snouting." (errata por "shouting") y "I know only one pure boat-song, the fine lyric, "Michael row the boat ashore" (No. 31)", y sigue con la nota del señor Ware de que "two measures are to be sung to each stroke".

caption.en: Page xvi of Slave Songs of the United States (New York, 1867), where William Francis Allen calls "Michael row the boat ashore" the only "pure boat-song" he knew and Charles Pickard Ware explains that two measures were sung to each stroke of the oars.
caption.es: Página xvi de Slave Songs of the United States (Nueva York, 1867), donde William Francis Allen llama a "Michael row the boat ashore" la única "pure boat-song" (auténtica canción de barca) que conocía, y Charles Pickard Ware explica que se cantaban dos compases por cada palada.

source: William Francis Allen, Charles Pickard Ware and Lucy McKim Garrison, eds., Slave Songs of the United States (New York: A. Simpson & Co., 1867), introduction, p. xvi (top of the page)
library: Smithsonian Libraries (digitized for the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1867; editors died 1889 (Allen), 1921 (Ware) and 1877 (Garrison). Internet Archive record (https://archive.org/metadata/slavesongsofunit00alle), possible-copyright-status: "Not in copyright. The Library knows of no copyright restrictions on this item." Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Smithsonian Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "31. MICHAEL ROW THE BOAT ASHORE.": two short lines of music in 2/4 with three flats, the first under "1. Michael row de boat a-shore, Hal-le-lu-jah!", the second in two parts under "2. Mich-ael boat a gos-pel boat, Hal-le-lu-jah!".
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "31. MICHAEL ROW THE BOAT ASHORE.": dos líneas cortas de música en 2/4 con tres bemoles, la primera bajo "1. Michael row de boat a-shore, Hal-le-lu-jah!" y la segunda a dos voces bajo "2. Mich-ael boat a gos-pel boat, Hal-le-lu-jah!".

caption.en: No. 31 on page 23 of Slave Songs of the United States (New York, 1867), the song's earliest known printing: the tune in E-flat on two short lines of music, the second printed in two parts.
caption.es: El n.º 31 en la página 23 de Slave Songs of the United States (Nueva York, 1867), la primera impresión conocida de la canción: la melodía en Mi bemol en dos líneas cortas de música, la segunda impresa a dos voces.

source: William Francis Allen, Charles Pickard Ware and Lucy McKim Garrison, eds., Slave Songs of the United States (New York: A. Simpson & Co., 1867), p. 23, No. 31, "Michael Row the Boat Ashore" (the heading and the two lines of music only)
